name: RUN!!! IV
summary: Unresolved. A revised core-first route collects all 999 required chips and reaches (28,4) alive at tick 4755, with complete native C trace parity. Chip has not reached the Exit; no winning replay or impossibility proof has been established.
proofSteps: MS supplies a default player at (0,0) despite the missing Chip tile. The surrounding chips initially separate the outer shell from the central monster moat.
A TypeScript candidate reached 892 collected chips, but its encoded replay dies in the native C engine at tick 2948. That candidate is not a valid MS solution.

The first native/TypeScript divergence occurs at tick 16: a Teeth at (12,23) attempts to move east into Empty over CloneMachine at (13,23). Native rejects the move; TypeScript permits it. The random states and selected eastward direction agree.

A reduced board reproduces the discrepancy without cloning or randomness. The correction uses the existing MS catalog entry policy and passes the reduced regression, preserves bowling-ball and Pet Carrier cloner behavior, and matches the entire original 2949-step native trace. That original route now correctly fails in both engines; it remains unsuitable as a solution.
limitations: No winning replay or universal impossibility proof has been established.

The earlier candidate that relied on the buried-cloner mismatch is invalid. An earlier 997-chip prefix has complete native trace parity, but its explored continuations did not win. Earlier checkpoints remain available for alternate continuations.

The preserved-gate prefix leaves two chips beside the exit, but the crowded core prevents any currently established route to use them. Its matching native trace does not establish improved solvability.

The zero-chip northeast-lure prefix has complete native trace parity, but its direct and east-waypoint return searches did not reach the Exit. Other routes and earlier checkpoints remain under investigation; collecting every required chip is not completion.

experiments.result: Decoded both 1024-cell DAT planes and exact level metadata; initialized production MS runtime and rendered actual game sprites.

experiments.method: Nearest-chip route with a four-tick survival check for each next action; one seed and stepping setting, no seed/parameter sweep.
experiments.result: Unverified TypeScript-only observation, superseded by the native mismatch below. 167 chips collected by tick 667;832 remain. Stopped at (24,5) after all five local four-tick movement/wait choices were lethal. This does not establish impossibility.

Unverified TypeScript-only observation, superseded by the native mismatch below. TypeScript runtime: 668 chips collected, 331 required chips remaining, alive at (2,17), tick 2931. The runtime listed 196 creatures in total, including Chip and the ball outside the moat; 194 were in the moat. Exact inputs are preserved in 932-shell-probe.json.

Unverified TypeScript-only observation, superseded by the native mismatch below. Entering (5,17) at tick 2940 dies at 2944. Waiting four ticks, entering at 2944 and retreating at 2948 survives; the saved prefix reaches (1,17) at tick 2963 with 330 chips required. This is not a complete replay and has not yet received native certification.

Encoded TypeScript replay matches manual simulation for the first 400 ticks. Native differs first at tick 16, then the candidate dies at tick 2948. Reduced native probe at tick 8 retains Teeth at (5,5), while the TypeScript regression fails with Teeth at (6,5).

The reduced engine test failed before the correction and passed afterward. All 269 tests across six nearby engine/catalog/controller suites passed. MS typecheck passed. Initial state, all 2949 steps, and result of the original replay match native with no differences, empty stderr, and identical replay bytes.

After collecting the protected outer shell and most outer boundary chips, Chip enters the core through (9,16). Retained chips at (10,15), (10,17), and (11,16) isolate the entry corridor while the rest of the interior is collected. Native and TypeScript agree on the initial state, all 4404 steps, and the result: alive at (11,15), tick 4403, with 40 chips required. Native stderr is empty and replay bytes are identical.

experiments.kind: split-visit core route with preserved chip barriers
experiments.result: An early visit collects core perimeter chips, then returns through the bottom double-chip airlock before the moat becomes crowded. After collecting the outer shell and most of its boundary, Chip returns to the core, collects the protected interior, and takes seven additional chips while retaining the remaining barrier layers. Native and TypeScript agree on the initial state, all 4612 steps, and the result: alive at (18,19), tick 4611, with 35 chips required. Native stderr is empty and replay bytes are identical. Subsequent bounded cleanup attempts are exploratory and do not establish impossibility.

After the native-certified split-visit checkpoint, collecting the right border before opening the north border reaches 997 collected chips. Native and TypeScript agree on the initial state, all 4836 steps, and the result: alive at (11,15), tick 4835, with 2 chips required. Native stderr is empty and replay bytes are identical. The bounded continuation search did not complete the level; this prefix is not a solution or an impossibility proof.

A revised right-border-first route retains the double chip at (16,13), directly north of the Socket-over-Exit at (16,14). A late N/W/N sequence collects the formerly preserved Walker outlet at (9,17), reaching (9,16) at tick 4807 with 2 chips required. Both chips at (16,13) remain available. Manual play, encoded TypeScript replay, and native C agree on all 4808 steps; initial state and result also match, replay bytes are identical, and native stderr is empty. This is an alternate 997-chip prefix, not a winning replay. A bounded continuation allowing the last two gate chips exhausted its explored frontier without completing.

A deterministic route joins five perimeter cycles into a path through 531 safe outer cells and uses paired bounces to collect stacked chips. It collects all 646 safe outer chip units in 683 moves, including (22,31); the earlier greedy route took 704 moves and skipped that tile. Native C and TypeScript agree on the initial state, all 3144 steps, and the result: alive at (31,30), tick 3143, with 269 chips required (730 collected). Original MS command audit and exact replay byte roundtrip pass; native stderr is empty. This is a partial route. Its subsequent bounded boundary-collection attempt reached 192 required at tick 3743, then exhausted the explored frontier without establishing a return or completion.

experiments.kind: protected exit gate and Teeth-lure refinements
experiments.result: The actual Exit is at (16,14), below a Socket. Preserving one or both chips at (16,13) permits a possible final collection beside it, but bounded right-first cleanup attempts still did not complete. Inside-core northwest/northeast lures changed Teeth facing without draining their packed border: a retained chip blocks the horizontal choice and alignment with Chip removes the vertical fallback. A proposed outside northwest lure would supply both northward and westward choices; it remains unproved. A north airlock at (16,11) preserves a chip behind Chip, but the tested exit through (16,10) did not pass the moving Glider traffic in the next row. These failures do not establish impossibility. The neighboring double-chip portal at (15,11) reaches (15,9) in a direct probe, but that state dies before the next move; a bounded search preserving the portal chip also found no safe exit (760 expansions, 100 move-depth limit). At that checkpoint the full outside lure remained untested. Later work deliberately opened several north cells and established an escape, but its tested return paths failed; this does not rule out other routes.

An earlier route clears the central area, then escapes through the alternative double-chip gate at (5,20), reaching (4,20) at tick 1359 with 721 chips required. Safe outer collection reaches 75 required at tick 4115. Clearing the outer boundary in bottom/left/top/right order reaches zero required chips. A subsequent explicit northeast lure reaches (28,4) alive at tick 4755. Manual play, encoded TypeScript replay and native C agree on all 4756 steps, including initial state and result; original MS input audit and exact replay-byte checks pass. This remains a partial route: bounded return attempts have not reached the Exit.
